items.title: The First Law of Complexodynamics
items.authors: Scott Aaronson
items.kind: Essay / blog post (not a research paper)
items.license: Link only; no explicit redistribution permission found.
items.scope: Rule 30 and mixing are toy illustrations. They do not prove a physical law, and apparent complexity is not Shannon entropy.

items.title: The Unreasonable Effectiveness of Recurrent Neural Networks
items.authors: Andrej Karpathy
items.kind: Tutorial / blog post (not a research paper)
items.license: Link only; no explicit redistribution permission found.
items.scope: The synthetic-text Notebook demonstrates a character RNN; it does not reproduce the tutorial's real-text experiments or measure language understanding.

items.title: Understanding LSTM Networks
items.authors: Christopher Olah; original LSTM paper by Sepp Hochreiter and Jürgen Schmidhuber
items.kind: Tutorial (not the original LSTM research paper)
items.license: Link only; no explicit redistribution permission found.
items.scope: Gates can help preserve useful state and gradients but do not guarantee arbitrary long-term memory.

items.title: Recurrent Neural Network Regularization
items.authors: Wojciech Zaremba, Ilya Sutskever, and Oriol Vinyals
items.license: Link only; arXiv's default non-exclusive distribution license is not a general permission to rehost the PDF.
items.scope: The paper applies dropout on non-recurrent connections. A repeated temporal mask is a distinct design choice and needs separate attribution.

items.title: Keeping Neural Networks Simple by Minimizing the Description Length of the Weights
items.authors: Geoffrey Hinton and Drew van Camp
items.license: Link only. ACM allows limited personal/classroom non-commercial copying; public server redistribution requires permission.
items.scope: The 1993 MDL method is not modern magnitude pruning. The Notebook combines related methods; cite pruning sources separately.

items.title: Pointer Networks
items.authors: Oriol Vinyals, Meire Fortunato, and Navdeep Jaitly
items.license: Link only; no broad redistribution grant found.
items.scope: A pointer selects variable-sized input positions. It does not itself make the encoder permutation-invariant or guarantee generalization.

items.title: ImageNet Classification with Deep Convolutional Neural Networks
items.authors: Alex Krizhevsky, Ilya Sutskever, and Geoffrey Hinton
items.license: Link only; no explicit permission to rehost the PDF found.
items.scope: Synthetic images and a scaled network are not an ImageNet reproduction. Keep the paper's LSVRC 2010 evaluation separate from its later 2012 competition result.

items.title: Order Matters: Sequence to Sequence for Sets
items.authors: Oriol Vinyals, Samy Bengio, and Manjunath Kudlur
items.license: Link only; no broad redistribution grant found.
items.scope: The Notebook's broad read-process-write framing is a teaching abstraction. Its forward-pass examples do not demonstrate a learned model or the paper's full experiments.

items.title: GPipe: Efficient Training of Giant Neural Networks using Pipeline Parallelism
items.authors: Yanping Huang et al.
items.license: Link only; no broad redistribution grant found.
items.scope: The single-process simulation explains scheduling ideas; it does not demonstrate multi-device throughput or the paper's speedups.

items.title: Deep Residual Learning for Image Recognition
items.authors: Kaiming He, Xiangyu Zhang, Shaoqing Ren, and Jian Sun
items.license: Link only; no broad redistribution grant found.
items.scope: Skip connections can ease optimization; they do not guarantee gradients never vanish or reproduce the paper's ImageNet experiments.

items.title: Multi-Scale Context Aggregation by Dilated Convolutions
items.authors: Fisher Yu and Vladlen Koltun
items.license: Link only; no broad redistribution grant found.
items.scope: The paper targets dense prediction and semantic segmentation; one dilated-convolution operator is not the full paper model.

items.title: Neural Message Passing for Quantum Chemistry
items.authors: Justin Gilmer et al.
items.license: PMLR articles are published under the CC BY 4.0 author agreement. An unmodified PDF is included at [pdfs/P12.pdf](pdfs/P12.pdf) with attribution.
items.scope: The toy implementation is not the paper's quantum-chemistry experiment or QM9 reproduction.

items.title: Attention Is All You Need
items.authors: Ashish Vaswani et al.
items.license: Link only; no broad redistribution grant found.
items.scope: The original paper uses an encoder–decoder for sequence transduction. Causal self-attention is a related autoregressive language-model setup, not the entire original architecture.

items.title: Neural Machine Translation by Jointly Learning to Align and Translate
items.authors: Dzmitry Bahdanau, Kyunghyun Cho, and Yoshua Bengio
items.license: Link only; no broad redistribution grant found.
items.scope: This is additive attention over an RNN encoder–decoder, not Transformer self-attention. The synthetic translation task is not the paper experiment.

items.title: Identity Mappings in Deep Residual Networks
items.authors: Kaiming He, Xiangyu Zhang, Shaoqing Ren, and Jian Sun
items.license: Link only; no broad redistribution grant found.
items.scope: The paper analyzes identity skip paths and post-add activations; pre-activation is a complete block design, not just moving ReLU before a convolution.

items.title: A Simple Neural Network Module for Relational Reasoning
items.authors: Adam Santoro et al.
items.license: Link only; no broad redistribution grant found.
items.scope: The toy task demonstrates a relation-network architecture; it does not establish general reasoning or reproduce the full evaluations.

items.title: Variational Lossy Autoencoder
items.authors: Xi Chen, Diederik P. Kingma et al.
items.license: Link only; no broad redistribution grant found.
items.scope: The Notebook primarily teaches a standard VAE; the linked paper combines global latent variables with an autoregressive decoder to capture global structure and leave details lossy.

items.title: Relational Recurrent Neural Networks
items.authors: Adam Santoro, Ryan Faulkner, David Raposo, Jack Rae, Mike Chrzanowski, Theophane Weber, Daan Wierstra, Oriol Vinyals, Razvan Pascanu, and Timothy Lillicrap
items.license: Link only; no broad redistribution grant found.
items.scope: The notebook implements selected relational-memory components and experiments on toy tasks; it is not the paper's full training and benchmark suite.

items.title: Quantifying the Rise and Fall of Complexity in Closed Systems: The Coffee Automaton
items.authors: Scott Aaronson et al.
items.kind: Research paper with a later author correction
items.license: Link only; no broad redistribution grant found.
items.scope: Read Aaronson's correction before treating the interacting coffee-automaton experiment as evidence: he reported a serious experimental error. The Notebook's extra thermodynamics topics are separate illustrations, not verified results of the paper.

items.title: Neural Turing Machines
items.authors: Alex Graves, Greg Wayne, and Ivo Danihelka
items.license: Link only; no broad redistribution grant found.
items.scope: The copy task teaches differentiable read/write; it is not the paper's full training setup or evidence of general algorithmic ability.

items.title: Deep Speech 2: End-to-End Speech Recognition in English and Mandarin
items.authors: Dario Amodei et al.
items.license: PMLR articles are published under the CC BY 4.0 author agreement. An unmodified PDF is included at [pdfs/P21.pdf](pdfs/P21.pdf) with attribution.
items.scope: The Notebook demonstrates CTC mechanics on synthetic features; it does not reproduce Deep Speech 2 with real speech or large-scale training.

items.title: Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models
items.authors: Jared Kaplan et al.
items.license: Link only; no broad redistribution grant found.
items.scope: Synthetic curves illustrate fitting/extrapolation, not the paper's empirical measurements. Chinchilla is later work by Hoffmann et al. (2022), not a Kaplan result; see the related source link.

items.title: The Minimum Description Length Principle
items.authors: Peter Grünwald; the Notebook also cites Jorma Rissanen's foundational article
items.kind: Book plus foundational article (not a single paper)
items.license: Link only; book and Elsevier article are copyrighted; no redistribution permission found.
items.scope: MDL depends on a specified coding scheme and model class. It is related to, but not identical to, uncomputable Kolmogorov complexity.

items.title: Machine Super Intelligence
items.authors: Shane Legg
items.source_label: Thesis PDF hosted by the author
items.license: Link only; no explicit reuse license found.
items.scope: Exact Solomonoff induction and AIXI are uncomputable. Monte Carlo/MCTS toys are approximations; takeoff simulations are thought experiments, not validated forecasts.

items.title: An Introduction to Kolmogorov Complexity and Its Applications
items.authors: Ming Li and Paul Vitányi
items.license: Link only; copyrighted book, no redistribution permission found.
items.scope: A compressor's length is an upper bound for that encoding, not exact Kolmogorov complexity; finite incompressibility is not proof of algorithmic randomness.

items.title: CS231n: Convolutional Neural Networks for Visual Recognition
items.authors: Stanford CS231n course staff
items.license: Link only; no course-site asset reuse license found.
items.scope: This is an abbreviated NumPy tutorial, not Stanford's full course. Synthetic images are not CIFAR-10/ImageNet results; the original course expects calculus, linear algebra, statistics, and ML background.

items.title: Better & Faster Large Language Models via Multi-token Prediction
items.authors: Fabian Gloeckle, Badr Youbi Idrissi, Baptiste Rozière, David Lopez-Paz, and Gabriel Synnaeve
items.license: The source identifies CC BY 4.0. An unmodified PDF is included at [pdfs/P27.pdf](pdfs/P27.pdf) with attribution.
items.scope: The paper uses independent future-token heads over a shared Transformer trunk. The small RNN/synthetic-text Notebook does not reproduce large-model benchmarks or inference-speed claims.

items.title: Dense Passage Retrieval for Open-Domain Question Answering
items.authors: Vladimir Karpukhin et al.
items.license: ACL materials published since 2016 are licensed under CC BY 4.0. An unmodified PDF is included at [pdfs/P28.pdf](pdfs/P28.pdf) with attribution.
items.scope: The simple random-initialized RNN encoder is not the paper's trained BERT-based DPR system. Do not claim DPR quality without a real training/evaluation run.

items.title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks
items.authors: Patrick Lewis et al.
items.license: Link only; no broad redistribution grant found.
items.scope: The simple retriever/generator illustrates the architecture; it does not reproduce the original DPR, BART, Wikipedia-index training/evaluation setup.

items.title: Lost in the Middle: How Language Models Use Long Contexts
items.authors: Nelson F. Liu, Kevin Lin, John Hewitt, Ashwin Paranjape, Michele Bevilacqua, Fabio Petroni, and Percy Liang
items.license: The source identifies CC BY 4.0. An unmodified PDF is included at [pdfs/P30.pdf](pdfs/P30.pdf) with attribution.
items.scope: The paper evaluates multi-document QA and key/value retrieval on real models. The synthetic position curve illustrates evaluation design, not the paper's findings.
